messages.content:
The test failure is related to a TAR archive checksum validation for "COMPRESS-335.tar". The current issue report states that the TAR file has a checksum with zero padding on the left instead of the typical NULL-SPACE termination on the right, which causes the last two digits of the checksum to be lost and thereby falsely treating the otherwise correct checksum as invalid.

The test method `testCOMPRESS335()` uses `getStreamFor("COMPRESS-335.tar")` to presumably create a `TarArchiveInputStream` from the file and reads the entries.

The checksum issue mentioned relates to how the TAR input stream reads and validates the checksum from the TAR header blocks. The TAR header contains a checksum field stored as 6 octal digits followed by space or NULL termination. The bug report suggests the current implementation expects the checksum to be right-aligned with trailing zeros replaced by NULL or space but the failing TAR archive has left-padded zeros instead, and those trailing digits are incorrectly discarded.

I attempted to locate TAR checksum reading or validation methods in `TarArchiveInputStream` but no exact checksum method was located. This suggests the checksum reading is implemented inline or inside another method.

The constructor of `TarArchiveInputStream` simply sets up input stream, encoding, and block/record sizes without checksum processing. The test calls `getNextEntry()` which calls `getNextTarEntry()` internally. The checksum validation should be around reading the header in `getNextTarEntry()`.

Next, I will retrieve the code for `TarArchiveInputStream.getNextTarEntry()` to inspect the header reading and checksum validation logic to confirm how the TAR checksum is read and validated, especially how it reads and sums the checksum field. This will likely reveal why left padding zeros cause checksum failure and if restricting to first 6 octal digits is necessary.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
